content: The vaginal ring should not remain in place for more than three months. If inserted correctly, it should not be felt and will not interfere with sexual activity. If you can feel the ring or experience slight discomfort, it may not be positioned high enough in the vagina. If the ring falls out, rinse it with lukewarm water and reinsert it. To remove the ring, hook your finger through it and gently pull it out. If you encounter difficulty removing the ring, contact your doctor. Dispose of the used ring in the trash. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause serious, potentially fatal complications such as blood clots (e.g., heart attack, stroke, pulmonary embolism, or deep vein thrombosis). Vaginal rings have also been associated, though rarely, with severe bacterial infections like toxic shock syndrome (TSS). Severe allergic reactions to this product are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice. Before using estradiol, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco, as it increases the risk of blood clots, especially when using estrogen products. Inform your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be immobile for an extended period (e.g., long flights), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin or face (melasma), which can worsen with sun exposure. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. If you develop a vaginal infection while using the ring, it can remain in place during treatment. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Discuss the risks and benefits of using this medication while breastfeeding with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. In case of overdose, this medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular physical exams, including lab and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted while using this medication. Follow your doctor’s instructions for breast self-exams and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Preventing or managing high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes can reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help control or prevent these conditions. Engage in mental exercises (e.g., reading, solving puzzles) to help prevent dementia. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not remove the ring from its pouch until ready for use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
